title: Sansera Engineering Revenue Jumps 33% on Aerospace and Semiconductor Surge
excerpt: The Bangalore-based precision engineering company reported Rs 1,021 crore in Q1 FY27 revenue, with its aerospace, defense, and semiconductor division emerging as the key growth driver.
body:
• Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue jumped 33% year-on-year to Rs 1,021.3 crore; net profit rose 39% to Rs 87.4 crore, driven by international and non-auto segment growth.
  • The Aerospace, Defence, and Semiconductor (ADS) segment delivered Rs 315.5 crore in FY26 revenue — up 155% year-on-year — with management guiding Rs 550-600 crore for FY27 and an unexecuted order backlog of Rs 4,463.8 crore.
  • Sansera won a landmark Airbus Defence and Space contract worth approximately $18.8 million — the first time Airbus selected an Indian supplier for a critical airborne medical evacuation system.
  • The company targets Rs 8,000-10,000 crore in revenue by FY30, with 40% from non-auto segments, and has entered mass production for semiconductor equipment components.

Q1 FY27: Breakout Quarter

Sansera Engineering, the Bangalore-based precision component manufacturer, reported consolidated revenue of Rs 1,021.3 crore for the first quarter of FY27 — a 33% increase from Rs 766.3 crore in Q1 FY26. Net profit climbed 39% to Rs 87.4 crore, up from Rs 63 crore in the year-ago period. The results, announced on August 12, were powered by strong growth in international and non-automotive segments.

The quarter builds on a strong FY26, which CEO B R Preetham described as "an inflection point" for the company. Full-year revenue rose 16% to Rs 3,498 crore, while profit after tax surged over 50% to Rs 327 crore.

"FY26 marked an inflection point in the company's journey despite global tariff disruptions, geopolitical volatility and export headwinds in select segments."

— B R Preetham, Executive Director & CEO, Sansera Engineering

The ADS Engine

At the center of Sansera's transformation is its Aerospace, Defence, and Semiconductor (ADS) vertical. The segment recorded Rs 315.5 crore in revenue during FY26 — a 155% year-on-year increase — with quarterly ADS sales reaching Rs 109.7 crore in Q4 FY26 alone. Management has guided for Rs 550-600 crore in ADS revenue for FY27, nearly doubling the FY26 base.

The unexecuted ADS order backlog stood at Rs 4,463.8 crore as of March 2026, providing multi-year revenue visibility. To underscore the strategic weight of this business, Sansera appointed Hari Krishnan as Executive Director and CEO of the ADS division on the same day it released Q1 results — giving the segment dedicated C-suite leadership for the first time.

Breaking Into Aerospace

Sansera's aerospace push took a concrete step forward with a long-term contract with Airbus Defence and Space worth approximately Rs 160 crore ($18.8 million) for the manufacture, supply, and support of the Airborne Intensive Care Transport Module (ICTM) for light and medium transport aircraft. The deal marks the first time Airbus has selected an Indian supplier for this critical airborne medical evacuation system.

The company has expanded its capability to produce complex aerospace parts and is operationalizing a dedicated aerospace facility. International business posted its highest-ever quarterly topline during Q4 FY26, with exports to the US rising 25.9% year-on-year and Sweden operations reporting record sales of Rs 77 crore, up 60% year-on-year.

Semiconductor: From Lab to Factory Floor

Sansera has moved from qualification to mass production in semiconductor equipment component manufacturing. The transition required significant capital investment: the company built advanced machining facilities, a Level 1000 clean room, and specialized quality systems to meet the exacting standards of chip fabrication equipment.

Goldman Sachs, which rates the stock a Buy with a target price of Rs 4,130, argues that global chip-equipment manufacturers have structural reasons to shift sourcing toward India, and that Sansera is positioned to capture a growing share of that business. Nomura has set its target at Rs 4,278, citing strong order wins and improving growth outlook.

"Sansera has spent nearly a decade preparing for its harvesting phase — a shift from being purely a legacy auto-components supplier toward machining precision parts for global semiconductor equipment makers."

— Goldman Sachs research note

Road to Rs 10,000 Crore

Sansera's long-term roadmap targets Rs 8,000-10,000 crore in revenue by FY30, with 40% of the mix coming from non-auto and tech-agnostic segments — up from about 18.5% in Q4 FY26. ADS margins are expected to reach 25-30% at full capacity utilization, well above the company's current consolidated EBITDA margin of around 20%.

Capital expenditure of approximately Rs 510 crore is planned for FY27, with investments focused on expanding ADS capacity and ramping up the Pantnagar facility for two-wheeler crankshaft production — a plant that could generate Rs 500 crore in annual revenue by itself. A joint venture with Japan's Nichidai Corporation, with an approved investment of up to Rs 50 crore, aims to manufacture advanced precision forged components for global markets.

What's Next

With Goldman Sachs forecasting EPS growth of 39% in FY27 and EBITDA margin expansion from 18.1% to 21.6% through FY29, the outlook centers on execution. The ADS order backlog, a dedicated division CEO, and ongoing capacity investments suggest Sansera is positioning itself not just as another auto-components maker riding a cycle, but as a precision engineering firm building structural advantages in aerospace and semiconductor supply chains that global OEMs are actively diversifying into India.
